concepts.name: NHRC: composition, appointment, powers and functions
concepts.description: The composition, appointment, tenure and service conditions of the National Human Rights Commission, its civil-court-like powers, its investigative machinery and its ten functions.
concepts.idea: The NHRC is a statutory watchdog with a judicial-heavy composition, a six-member selection committee and civil-court-like inquiry powers, but only recommendatory force.
concepts.rule: The NHRC is a statutory body under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. It has a Chairperson (retired Chief Justice of India or Supreme Court Judge), five full-time members (a Supreme Court judge, a High Court Chief Justice and three human rights experts, one a woman) and seven ex-officio members. The President appoints on the recommendation of a six-member committee headed by the Prime Minister; the term is three years or age 70 and re-appointment is allowed, and salary is fixed by the Central Government. It has civil-court powers, may use central and state officers and has a nucleus of investigating staff, and performs ten functions, from inquiry and court intervention to research and encouraging NGOs. The 2019 Amendment widened the chair, added experts and ex-officio members and cut the term from five to three years.
concepts.example: A newspaper report on a custodial death reaches the NHRC: it can take it up suo motu, summon the officers, borrow a state investigating team and recommend compensation, but cannot punish the guilty itself.

questions.q: The National Human Rights Commission has a few ex-officio members besides its full-time Chairperson and members. Which one of the following is NOT among its ex-officio members?
questions.a: Chairperson of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
o: Chairperson of the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis
Chairperson of the National Commission for Women
Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
questions.e: Under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (as amended in 2019), the ex-officio members are seven: the chairpersons of the National Commissions for Minorities, SCs, STs, Women, Backward Classes and Protection of Child Rights, and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities. The National Commission for Safai Karamcharis is not in that list.
w: The Chairperson of the National Commission for Women is an ex-officio member.
The Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities is the seventh ex-officio member.
The Chairperson of the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights is an ex-officio member.

questions.q: The Chairperson and members of the NHRC are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee. Which one of the following is NOT a member of that committee?
o: Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha
Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha
questions.e: The six-member committee is the Prime Minister (head), the Lok Sabha Speaker, the Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman, the Leaders of the Opposition of both Houses and the Union Home Minister. The Chief Justice of India is only consulted when a sitting Supreme Court judge or a sitting High Court Chief Justice is to be appointed.
w: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is a member of the six-member committee.
The Leaders of the Opposition in both Houses sit on the committee.
The Union Home Minister is the sixth member of the committee.

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the legal basis and the mandate of the National Human Rights Commission?
questions.a: A statutory body created by an Act of Parliament in 1993 that guards the rights of life, liberty, equality and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in international covenants
o: A statutory body created by an Act of Parliament in 1993 that guards the rights of life, liberty, equality and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in international covenants
A constitutional body created by an Article inserted in 1993 that guards only the fundamental rights listed in Part III
A body set up in 1993 by a Cabinet resolution to look after the rights contained in international covenants
A statutory body of 1993 that watches over rights arising only from the Constitution and not from international covenants
questions.e: The NHRC is a statutory, not constitutional, body set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. Its watch covers rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in international covenants and enforceable by courts in India.
w: It has no constitutional Article behind it and its mandate is not confined to Part III; it is a statutory body.
It was created by the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, not by an executive resolution.
Its mandate expressly includes rights embodied in international covenants such as the ICCPR and ICESCR.

questions.q: While inquiring into a complaint, the NHRC has powers similar to those of a civil court. Which one of the following, however, is NOT a power the Commission has?
questions.a: Punishing a public servant it finds guilty of violating human rights
o: Punishing a public servant it finds guilty of violating human rights
Summoning and enforcing the attendance of a person from any part of India
Receiving evidence on affidavits and requiring the discovery and production of documents
Requisitioning any public record from a court or a public office
questions.e: The Commission has civil-court-like inquiry powers (summons, discovery, affidavits, requisitioning records) but it can only recommend compensation, prosecution or disciplinary action; it has no power to punish violators.
w: Summoning and enforcing attendance anywhere in India is a civil-court-like power it has.
Discovery, production of documents and evidence on affidavits are among its powers.
Requisitioning a public record from a court or office is among its powers.

questions.q: Who determines the salary, allowances and other conditions of service of the Chairperson and members of the National Human Rights Commission?
questions.a: The Central Government, but they cannot be varied to the disadvantage of the person after appointment
o: The Central Government, but they cannot be varied to the disadvantage of the person after appointment
Parliament, by a provision in the Second Schedule, and they can be revised downwards only by an amendment
The President on the recommendation of the selection committee, and they may be revised during the term
The Finance Commission, which also charges them to the Consolidated Fund of India
questions.e: The salary, allowances and other conditions of service of the Chairperson and members are determined by the Central Government but cannot be varied to the disadvantage of a member after appointment.
w: The Second Schedule does not cover the Commission; the Central Government fixes these conditions.
The Central Government fixes them and they cannot be varied to the member's disadvantage.
The Finance Commission has no such role; the Central Government fixes them.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the National Human Rights Commission:

1. The Chairperson must be a retired Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. A serving Supreme Court Judge cannot be a member; only a retired Supreme Court Judge is eligible as the judicial member.
3. Three members are persons with knowledge or practical experience of human rights, and at least one of them must be a woman.
4. Any serving or retired Judge of a High Court can be the High Court member of the Commission.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The chair is a former CJI or Supreme Court judge. Statement 2 is incorrect: A serving or retired Supreme Court Judge qualifies as a member. Statement 3 is correct: Three non-judicial members, at least one a woman. Statement 4 is incorrect: The High Court member must be a serving or retired Chief Justice of a High Court, not any Judge. So the correct combination is 1 and 3 only.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of the Chairperson and members of the NHRC:

1. They are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a six-member committee headed by the Prime Minister.
2. The Chief Justice of India sits on the committee as one of its six members.
3. The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, rather than its Deputy Chairman, is a member of the committee.
4. A sitting Supreme Court Judge can be appointed as a member only after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The committee is six-member with the Prime Minister at its head. Statement 2 is incorrect: The CJI is not a member; he is only consulted for a sitting judge or sitting Chief Justice. Statement 3 is incorrect: The Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha is the member. Statement 4 is correct: Consultation with the CJI is required for a sitting judge or a sitting High Court Chief Justice. So the correct combination is 1 and 4 only.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the term and service conditions of the NHRC Chairperson and members:

1. The term of office is three years or till the age of 70, whichever is earlier.
2. They are eligible for re-appointment.
3. After their tenure they cannot take up further employment under the Central or a State government.
4. Their salary and allowances are fixed by the Central Government and cannot be changed to their disadvantage after appointment.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Term of three years or age 70. Statement 2 is correct: Re-appointment is permitted. Statement 3 is correct: Post-tenure employment under the Centre or a State is barred. Statement 4 is correct: Central Government fixes them, with no variation to disadvantage. So the correct combination is 1, 2, 3 and 4.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about how the NHRC investigates complaints:

1. It may use the services of any officer or investigation agency of the Central or a State government.
2. It can call for information or a report from the Central and State governments or from authorities subordinate to them.
3. The Commission has no investigating staff of its own and has to borrow every investigator it uses.
4. It can hold on-the-spot inquiries, including visits to jails.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the Commission can use the services of any officer or investigation agency of the Central or a State government. Statement 2 is correct: it may call for information or a report from them or from subordinate authorities. Statement 3 is incorrect: the Commission has its own nucleus of investigating staff (an investigation division headed by a police officer) and may also borrow officers. Statement 4 is correct: on-the-spot inquiries and jail visits are within its powers. So the correct combination is 1, 2 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect (it has its own investigating staff) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct (it may borrow officers or agencies).
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: the Commission may use officers or agencies of either government.
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: it may call for information or reports from governments and subordinate authorities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the inquiry and intervention functions of the NHRC:

1. Its inquiry into a violation is set in motion by a petition from the victim or someone acting for the victim, or by an order of a court; suo motu action is left to the courts.
2. Its inquiry covers violations of human rights, and negligence in preventing them, by public servants such as police and prison authorities.
3. It may intervene, with the approval of the court, in a proceeding on a human rights allegation pending before that court.
4. It can visit jails and detention places to study the living conditions of inmates and make recommendations.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It can also act suo motu, besides acting on a petition or on an order of a court. Statement 2 is correct: Violations by police, prison authorities and other public authorities are covered. Statement 3 is correct: Intervention in court proceedings is a function, with the court's approval. Statement 4 is correct: Jail and detention visits are a function. So the correct combination is 2, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the NHRC:

1. Section 12 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 lists ten functions of the Commission, the last being the undertaking of such other functions as it considers necessary for the promotion of human rights.
2. The Commission can try persons accused of violating human rights through special courts under its own control.
3. Encouraging the efforts of non-governmental organisations working in the field of human rights is one of its functions.
4. It reviews the factors, including acts of terrorism, that inhibit the enjoyment of human rights and recommends remedial measures.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Section 12 lists ten functions, ending with such other functions as the Commission considers necessary. Statement 2 is incorrect: Human Rights Courts are set up by the State government with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court (Section 30); the Commission only recommends. Statement 3 is correct: encouraging the efforts of NGOs is among the Section 12 functions. Statement 4 is correct: reviewing factors, including acts of terrorism, that inhibit human rights is also a Section 12 function. So the correct combination is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect (the Commission cannot try accused persons) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct (ten functions are listed in Section 12).
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: encouraging NGOs is a function.
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: reviewing factors such as terrorism that inhibit human rights is a function.

questions.q:
The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 changed the structure of the NHRC. Consider the following statements:

1. A person who has been a Judge of the Supreme Court, and not only a Chief Justice of India, is eligible to be appointed Chairperson.
2. The number of members chosen from persons with human rights knowledge or experience was raised from two to three, with at least one a woman.
3. The Chairpersons of the National Commission for Backward Classes, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities became ex-officio members.
4. The term of the Chairperson and members was raised from three years to five years.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the 2019 Amendment made any person who has been a Judge of the Supreme Court, not only a Chief Justice of India, eligible as Chairperson. Statement 2 is correct: the number of members from persons with human rights knowledge or experience rose from two to three, at least one a woman. Statement 3 is correct: the chairpersons of the National Commission for Backward Classes, the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities became ex-officio members. Statement 4 is incorrect: the term was reduced from five to three years and re-appointment was allowed. So the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (the term was cut from five to three years) and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: members with human rights knowledge rose from two to three.
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: any former Supreme Court Judge can now be Chairperson.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the working of the NHRC:

1. Its recommendations are binding on the government if it does not report back in time.
2. It organises camp sittings and open hearings in different parts of the country to bring justice to the doorstep of victims.
3. It can inquire directly into violations by members of the armed forces in the same manner as into violations by the police.
4. It has been described as a 'toothless tiger' because, despite civil-court-like powers, it can only recommend.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Recommendations are never binding; the government need only inform the Commission of action within one month. Statement 2 is correct: It organises camp sittings and open hearings in different parts of the country to bring justice to the doorstep of victims. Statement 3 is incorrect: For the armed forces it can only seek a report from the Central Government. Statement 4 is correct: Because it can only recommend and not enforce, the Commission is often criticised in this way. So the correct combination is 2 and 4 only.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the headquarters and procedure of the NHRC:

1. Its headquarters is at Delhi, and an office elsewhere in India can be opened only through a fresh Act of Parliament.
2. Its procedure is prescribed by the Central Government by rules, which the Commission merely follows.
3. It has all the powers of a civil court and its proceedings have a judicial character.
4. A request for information or a report from a State Government must be routed through the Central Government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It can itself establish offices in other places in India; no fresh Act is needed. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Commission is vested with the power to regulate its own procedure. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: It may call for information or reports from the Central and State governments directly. So the correct combination is 3 only.
w: '4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about removal and reporting in the case of the NHRC:

1. The President can remove a member who engages, during the term of office, in paid employment outside the duties of the office.
2. A member adjudged insolvent can be removed by the President only after the Supreme Court has held an inquiry and advised removal.
3. For proved misbehaviour or incapacity, the President must refer the matter to the Supreme Court and can remove the member only if the Court upholds the cause and advises so.
4. The annual and special reports of the Commission go to the Central Government and the State Government concerned, and are laid before the legislatures with a memorandum of action taken.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: paid employment outside office duties is a ground of removal by the President. Statement 2 is incorrect: insolvency is one of the five grounds on which the President removes directly; the Supreme Court reference is required only for proved misbehaviour or incapacity. Statement 3 is correct: the reference and the Court's advice are required. Statement 4 is correct: reports are laid before the respective legislatures with a memorandum of action taken and reasons for non-acceptance. So exactly 3 statements are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct, so three.
'All four' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: insolvency needs no Supreme Court inquiry.
'Only one' miscounts: three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the NHRC:

1. It reviews the constitutional and other legal safeguards for the protection of human rights and recommends measures for their effective implementation.
2. Study of treaties and international instruments on human rights is a function of the State Human Rights Commissions but not of the NHRC.
3. It undertakes and promotes research in the field of human rights.
4. It may visit jails only with the prior permission of the Supreme Court.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Function 4. Statement 2 is incorrect: Studying treaties and international instruments is a function of the NHRC. Statement 3 is correct: Function 7. Statement 4 is incorrect: No such permission is needed; visiting jails and detention places is itself a function. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 2019 Amendment to the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:

1. The Secretary-General of the NHRC exercises its administrative and financial powers, subject to the control of the Chairperson, but not its judicial functions or power to make regulations.
2. The Secretary of a State Human Rights Commission exercises its administrative and financial powers, subject to the control of the Chairperson.
3. The Central Government may confer on State Human Rights Commissions the human rights functions in Union Territories other than Delhi.
4. A person who has been a Judge of a High Court is made eligible to chair the NHRC.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct; Delhi's functions stay with the NHRC. Statement 4 is incorrect: That change applies to the State Human Rights Commission chair; the NHRC chair may be a former Supreme Court Judge. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The NHRC cannot punish those who violate human rights.
Statement-II: The NHRC has all the powers of a civil court and its proceedings have a judicial character.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Commission can only recommend compensation, prosecution or disciplinary action. Statement-II is correct, but having civil-court powers for inquiry does not explain why it cannot punish, so Statement-II does not explain Statement-I.
w: This option treats Statement-II as explaining Statement-I; check each statement against the provision first.
This option treats Statement-II as incorrect; check each statement against the provision first.
This option treats Statement-I as incorrect; check each statement against the provision first.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: After their tenure the Chairperson and members of the NHRC cannot take further employment under the Central or a State government.
Statement-II: The provisions on appointment, tenure, removal and conditions of service of the Commission are aimed at securing its autonomy, independence and impartiality.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: under Section 6 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, the Chairperson and members of the NHRC are ineligible for further employment under the Central or a State government after their tenure. Statement-II is correct, and the Act's provisions on appointment, tenure, removal and service conditions are meant to secure autonomy, independence and impartiality, which explains the bar on post-tenure employment.
w: This option treats Statement-II as correct but not explaining Statement-I; yet the bar on later government jobs is a safeguard meant to keep members independent.
This option treats Statement-II as incorrect; the Act's service provisions are in fact designed to secure autonomy, independence and impartiality.
This option treats Statement-I as incorrect; the Act does bar the Chairperson and members from further government employment.

questions.q:
Match the time limit or date in List-I with the figure in List-II (National Human Rights Commission)
List-I
A. Limit within which a matter must be taken up, counted from the alleged violation
B. Period within which the government should inform the Commission of action on its recommendations
C. Period within which the Centre should inform the Commission of action on recommendations concerning the armed forces
D. Year in which India acceded to the ICCPR and the ICESCR
List-II
1. Three months
2. 1979
3. One year
4. One month
questions.e: The Commission cannot inquire into a matter after one year from the alleged violation (A-3); the government should inform it of action within one month (B-4); for the armed forces the Centre should inform it within three months (C-1); India acceded to the two covenants on 10 April 1979 (D-2).
w: Swaps the one-year limitation period with the one-month reporting period.
Swaps the one-month period with the three-month armed-forces period.
Gives the armed forces the year 1979 and the accession the three-month period, which are not matched.

concepts.name: NHRC removal, reports and limits; the State Human Rights Commission
concepts.description: Removal of the NHRC Chairperson and members, the reports and limits of the Commission, the main criticisms made of it, and the composition, appointment, tenure, removal and jurisdiction of State Human Rights Commissions and Human Rights Courts.
concepts.idea: The NHRC is protected by a Supreme Court-inquiry removal procedure but is limited by recommendatory force, a one-year bar and a restricted role on the armed forces, while the SHRC mirrors it at State level with Governor appointing and President removing.
concepts.rule: The President can remove the NHRC chair or a member for insolvency, outside paid employment, infirmity, unsound mind declared by a court or conviction with imprisonment; for misbehaviour or incapacity a Supreme Court inquiry and advice come first. Reports go to the Centre and the State and are laid before the legislatures; for the armed forces the Commission can only seek a report and the Centre must act in three months; it cannot inquire after one year. Criticisms are pendency, staff shortage, executive dominance, over-judicialisation and weak follow-up. The SHRC has a chairperson (retired Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court) and two members, is appointed by the Governor on a committee led by the Chief Minister, serves three years or till 70, is removable only by the President, and inquires only into State and Concurrent List subjects.
concepts.example: A District Judge with eight years' service is appointed to a SHRC after the High Court Chief Justice is consulted; to remove her for misbehaviour the President must first refer the matter to the Supreme Court.

questions.q: The President wishes to remove a member of the National Human Rights Commission on the ground of proved misbehaviour. Which one of the following procedures must be followed?
questions.a: The President refers the matter to the Supreme Court and removes the member only if the Court upholds the charge and advises so
o: The President refers the matter to the Supreme Court and removes the member only if the Court upholds the charge and advises so
The President may remove the member on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers after giving the member a hearing on the charge
Both Houses of Parliament must pass a resolution by a special majority asking the President to remove the member
The selection committee that recommended the member must meet again and recommend the removal to the President
questions.e: For proved misbehaviour or incapacity the President has to refer the matter to the Supreme Court for an inquiry; only if the Court upholds the cause and advises removal can he remove the Chairperson or member. This is a safeguard under the 1993 Act.
w: Removal for misbehaviour needs a Supreme Court inquiry; Council of Ministers' advice alone is not enough.
The 1993 Act does not use a parliamentary address; the Supreme Court inquiry is the safeguard.
The selection committee has no role in removal.

questions.q: The President can remove the Chairperson or a member of the NHRC on certain grounds without a Supreme Court inquiry. Which one of the following is NOT such a ground?
questions.a: Acquiring a financial interest likely to affect prejudicially his official functions
o: Acquiring a financial interest likely to affect prejudicially his official functions
Engaging, during the term of office, in paid employment outside the duties of the office
Being of unsound mind and so declared by a competent court
questions.e: The NHRC grounds are insolvency, outside paid employment, infirmity of mind or body, unsound mind declared by a court, and conviction with a sentence of imprisonment. The financial-interest ground belongs to the Central Vigilance Commission, not the NHRC.
w: Insolvency is a listed ground.
Outside paid employment is a listed ground.
Unsound mind declared by a competent court is a listed ground.

questions.q: The Chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission has to be:
questions.a: A retired Chief Justice or a Judge of a High Court
o: A retired Chief Justice or a Judge of a High Court
A retired Judge of the Supreme Court who has served as a Chief Justice of a High Court
A retired Chief Justice of a High Court alone; a Judge of a High Court is not eligible
A District Judge of the State with at least seven years of service as District Judge
questions.e: The SHRC chairperson should be a retired Chief Justice or a Judge of a High Court; the 2019 Amendment added the Judge of a High Court.
w: The qualification is drawn from the High Court, not from the Supreme Court bench.
Per the 2019 Amendment a person who has been a Judge of a High Court is also eligible.
That is the qualification of one of the two members, not of the Chairperson.

questions.q: A District Judge can be appointed as a member of a State Human Rights Commission if he has a minimum experience as District Judge of:
questions.e: A member of the SHRC may be a serving or retired High Court Judge, or a District Judge of the State with a minimum of seven years' experience as District Judge.
w: The requirement is seven years, not five.
Ten years is not the requirement; it is seven.
Three years is the SHRC term of office, not the District Judge experience.

questions.q: The Chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission are appointed by the Governor. Who can remove them from office?

concepts.name: NHRC in practice; powers and functions of the State Human Rights Commission
concepts.description: NHRC case studies and criticisms (Chakma refugees, encounters, bonded labour), its limits and reforms, and the powers, functions, recommendations and reports of State Human Rights Commissions.
concepts.idea: The NHRC's record shows strong advocacy but weak enforcement, while the SHRC shares the civil-court powers and recommendatory force but works only on State and Concurrent List subjects.
concepts.rule: The NHRC filed the writ petition for about 65,000 Chakma refugees in Arunachal Pradesh, contributed to the police procedure on encounter deaths and to monitoring bonded labour, and looked into the Punjab mass cremations. It cannot penalise non-compliance, act against purely private parties, probe a complaint more than a year old, or inquire directly into the armed forces; reforms include an independent investigative cadre and, as GANHRI's Sub-Committee on Accreditation urged, publicised vacancies and broader consultation. A SHRC regulates its own procedure, has civil-court powers and judicial proceedings, may recommend compensation, prosecution, disciplinary action and interim relief, and may approach the High Court or Supreme Court. Its recommendations are not binding, but action taken must be reported within one month, and its reports go to the State Government and the State Legislature.
concepts.example: A State Commission finds that a police officer's negligence caused a custodial death: it can recommend compensation and prosecution and go to the High Court, but the State has only to report within a month.

questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: under Section 29 of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 the study-of-treaties function is omitted for the State Commission, leaving nine functions against ten. Statement 2 is correct: it encourages and supports the efforts of non-governmental organisations working in human rights. Statement 3 is correct: it can intervene, with the approval of the court, in a court proceeding involving a human rights allegation. Statement 4 is incorrect: the review covers factors including acts of terrorism, insurgency and extremism. So the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect (the review is not limited to terrorism) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: the review covers terrorism, insurgency and extremism.
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: the State Commission supports the efforts of NGOs.

4. Because staff are short, the Commission appoints retired Government officers as full-time members on contract.

Statement 4 is incorrect: It engages retired officers as consultants on contract, not as members. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.

'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the reports of a State Human Rights Commission:

3. The reports are laid before Parliament by the Governor.

Statement 3 is incorrect: they are laid before the State Legislature, not Parliament. questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission are appointed by the Governor, yet only the President can remove them.
Statement-II: For proved misbehaviour or incapacity the President may remove a member of a State Human Rights Commission on his own satisfaction, without any inquiry by the Supreme Court.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I

questions.e: Statement-I is correct: the Governor appoints the Chairperson and members of a State Human Rights Commission, but only the President can remove them. Statement-II is incorrect: for proved misbehaviour or incapacity the President must refer the matter to the Supreme Court for inquiry and may remove the member only if the Court upholds the cause and advises removal; the President cannot remove on his own satisfaction in such a case.
w: Statement-II is incorrect, so the two statements cannot both be correct and II cannot explain I: removal for misbehaviour needs a Supreme Court inquiry.
Statement-II is incorrect, so 'both correct' is wrong: the President cannot remove on his own satisfaction without a Supreme Court inquiry for misbehaviour or incapacity.
Statement-I is correct, not incorrect: the Governor appoints, but only the President can remove.

concepts.name: Lokpal origins and the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013
concepts.description: The global evolution of the Ombudsman, the Indian idea of Lokpal and the ten Bills, and the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 -- jurisdiction, composition, selection, powers, timelines and the Lokayukta mandate.
concepts.idea: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 is the tenth attempt at a statutory ombudsman, giving the Lokpal a defined composition, selection committee, powers over the CBI, strict timelines and a mandate for State Lokayuktas.
concepts.rule: The Ombudsman began in Sweden in 1809 (Finland 1919, Denmark 1955, New Zealand and Norway 1962, the UK 1967). In India the First ARC (1966-70) recommended the Lokpal and Lokayukta; the terms were coined by L. M. Singhvi; nine Bills lapsed or were withdrawn and the tenth became the Act of 2013. The Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to eight members, half judicial and half from the SC, ST, OBC, minority and women groups, selected by a committee of the Prime Minister, Speaker, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the CJI or nominee and an eminent jurist. It covers the Prime Minister with exclusions, Ministers, MPs and Group A-D officials, superintends the CBI for referred cases, and works to time limits of 3+3 months, 6+6 months and 1+1 year. States must set up Lokayuktas within 365 days.
concepts.example: A complaint against a Group B officer reaches the Lokpal: it can order a preliminary inquiry in three months, direct the CBI to investigate, attach the assets and sanction the prosecution.

questions.q: The Whyatt Report of 1961 recommended an Ombudsman-type office for which country?
questions.e: The Whyatt Report of 1961 (by the JUSTICE committee) preceded the Parliamentary Commissioner for Administration of Great Britain. New Zealand and Norway adopted the office in 1962 and Sweden has had it since 1809.
w: New Zealand adopted the office in 1962 and was not the subject of that report.
Norway adopted it in 1962; the report concerned Britain.
Sweden had the office since 1809, long before 1961.

questions.q: The terms 'Lokpal' and 'Lokayukta' for the Indian Ombudsman were coined by:
questions.e: Dr L. M. Singhvi coined the terms Lokpal and Lokayukta.
w: Sen, as Law Minister, floated the idea of an ombudsman in Parliament in the early 1960s but did not coin the terms.
Morarji Desai headed the First ARC that recommended the institutions, but did not coin the terms.
K. Santhanam headed the Committee on Prevention of Corruption behind the CVC.

questions.q: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 was the culmination of repeated attempts at legislation. Which of the Bills was finally enacted as the Act?
questions.a: The tenth Bill, introduced in December 2011
o: The tenth Bill, introduced in December 2011
The ninth Bill of August 2011, which was withdrawn
The eighth Bill of 2001, which lapsed in 2004
The seventh Bill of 1998, which lapsed with the 12th Lok Sabha
questions.e: Of the ten official attempts, the first four lapsed, the fifth was withdrawn, the sixth and seventh lapsed, the eighth (2001) lapsed in 2004 and the ninth (2011) was withdrawn; the tenth (December 2011) became the Act of 2013.
w: The ninth Bill was withdrawn by the Government.
The eighth Bill lapsed with the 13th Lok Sabha in 2004.
The seventh Bill lapsed with the dissolution of the 12th Lok Sabha.

questions.q: Under the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, the Chairperson and members of the Lokpal are selected through a Selection Committee. Which one of the following is NOT a member of that Committee?

o: Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha
Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by him
An eminent jurist nominated by the President
questions.e: The Selection Committee has the Prime Minister, the Lok Sabha Speaker, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the CJI or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by him, and an eminent jurist nominated by the President on the recommendation of the first four. The Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha is not a member.
w: The Lok Sabha Speaker is a member.
The CJI or his nominee is a member.
The eminent jurist is the fifth member.

questions.q: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 lays down timelines for dealing with a complaint. For the trial of a case before special courts the Act prescribes:
questions.a: One year, extendable by one year
o: One year, extendable by one year
Six months, extendable by six months
Three months, extendable by three months
Two years, extendable by one year
questions.e: Preliminary inquiry: three months, extendable by three months; investigation: six months, extendable by six months; trial through special courts: one year, extendable by one year.
w: That is the investigation timeline, not the trial period.
That is the timeline for the preliminary inquiry.
The trial period is one year, extendable by one year.

Consider the following statements about the jurisdiction of the Lokpal under the 2013 Act:

1. It covers the Prime Minister, Union Ministers, Members of Parliament and Group A, B, C and D officials of the Central Government.
2. It excludes Group C and Group D employees, who remain under departmental vigilance only.
3. It extends to bodies financed fully or partly by the Central Government and to entities receiving foreign donations of more than Rs 10 lakh a year.
4. It covers the Prime Minister, but matters of national security, foreign relations and public order are excluded.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It covers the Prime Minister, Union Ministers, Members of Parliament and Group A, B, C and D officials of the Central Government. Statement 2 is incorrect: Group C and D employees are covered; the CVC proceeds in their cases subject to Lokpal's reporting and review. Statement 3 is correct: It extends to bodies financed fully or partly by the Central Government and to entities receiving foreign donations of more than Rs 10 lakh a year. Statement 4 is correct. So the correct combination is 1, 3 and 4 only.

concepts.name: Lokpal drawbacks and the Central Bureau of Investigation
concepts.description: The shortcomings of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013, and the Central Bureau of Investigation -- origin, motto, mission, Director's appointment and tenure, functions, the Vineet Narain judgment and the State-consent rule.
concepts.idea: The Lokpal Act is weakened by procedural limits, while the CBI is a non-statutory agency of the DSPE Act, 1946 whose Director's tenure, selection and consent from States are the minute facts of the topic.
concepts.rule: The Lokpal cannot act suo motu, bars anonymous complaints, allows only a seven-year window and has a non-transparent procedure for the Prime Minister; it was constituted only in 2019. The CBI began as the Special Police Establishment (1941), was governed by the DSPE Act, 1946 and was set up as the CBI by a Home Ministry resolution in 1963; it is not a statutory body and works under the DoPT. The Director is selected by a committee of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the CJI or his nominee, with a fixed two-year tenure extendable by one year at a time up to five, and cannot be transferred without the committee's approval. After Vineet Narain (1997) superintendence in corruption cases passed to the CVC; the CBI needs a State's consent to operate there but can act on direction of the Supreme Court or a High Court.
concepts.example: A State withdraws general consent: the CBI cannot register a fresh case there without specific consent, but a High Court-ordered probe goes on and pending cases are unaffected.

questions.q: In 2014 the Supreme Court struck down Section 6A of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, which gave officers of the rank of Joint Secretary and above protection from even a preliminary inquiry by the CBI. The Court held that the provision violated:
questions.a: Article 14, because a corrupt officer's rank cannot place him in a protected class
o: Article 14, because a corrupt officer's rank cannot place him in a protected class
Article 16, because it denied equality of opportunity in public employment
Article 21, because it deprived victims of a fair investigation
Article 20, because it protected officers from double jeopardy
questions.e: A Constitution Bench held Section 6A, which shielded Joint Secretary-level and senior officers, violative of Article 14, noting that the status of a public servant does not exempt him from equal treatment.
w: The Constitution Bench relied on equality before law (Article 14), not Article 16.
The ruling rested on Article 14 and the equal treatment of corrupt public servants.

questions.q: The Central Bureau of Investigation traces its origin to the Special Police Establishment set up in 1941 to investigate bribery and corruption in transactions of which department during the Second World War?
questions.e: The Special Police Establishment (1941) investigated bribery in transactions with the War and Supply Department; the DSPE Act, 1946 transferred its superintendence to the Home Department and widened its work to all departments.
w: The Establishment's superintendence moved to the Home Department only with the DSPE Act of 1946.
It concerned war-time purchases and supplies, not the Railways.
The Establishment was under the War and Supply Department, not Finance.

questions.q: The Central Bureau of Investigation, though its powers flow from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946, functions under the administrative control of which authority?

o: The Department of Personnel and Training
The Ministry of Law and Justice

questions.q: Under the Delhi Special Police Establishment (Amendment) Act, 2021 the tenure of the CBI Director, which is fixed at two years, may be extended up to a maximum of:

w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.e: Statement-I is correct: this is widely reported, but it is a time-bound position, since some States later restored consent. But the Union Territory position is a separate legal fact and does not explain why particular States withdrew their general consent, so II does not explain I.
w: Statement-II is an independent fact about Union Territories; it does not explain why States withdrew consent, so 'explains' is wrong.
Statement-II is correct, not incorrect: the Central Government can extend the CBI's powers to Union Territories without any State's consent.

Consider the following statements:

o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

w: Statement-II is incorrect (appointment follows a committee's recommendation), so it cannot explain Statement-I.

concepts.name: Central Vigilance Commission
concepts.description: The Central Vigilance Commission -- origin and status, composition, term, organisation, removal, service conditions, functions, jurisdiction, working and the Whistle Blowers framework.
concepts.idea: The CVC is the apex statutory vigilance body: a Commissioner and up to two Vigilance Commissioners with UPSC-like status, superintending the CBI only in corruption investigations and advising rather than ordering the Government.
concepts.rule: The CVC began in 1964 by an executive resolution on the Santhanam Committee's recommendation and became statutory by the CVC Act, 2003. It has a Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than two Vigilance Commissioners, appointed by the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister, Home Minister and Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, for four years or age 65; their conditions match the UPSC Chairman and members. It has a Secretariat, a Chief Technical Examiners' Wing and Commissioners for Departmental Inquiries. Removal is by the President on insolvency, conviction involving moral turpitude, outside paid employment, infirmity or a harmful interest, and for misbehaviour only after a Supreme Court inquiry. It superintends the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases (not administration), reviews investigations and sanctions, advises the Government and is the designated agency for whistle-blower disclosures.
concepts.example: A bank officer of Scale V is accused of corruption: the CVC can call for a report, advise the Government, and if the Government rejects the advice it must record its reasons.

Statement 3 is correct: A Commissioner is deemed guilty of misbehaviour if he is concerned or interested in any contract or agreement made by the Central Government or shares its profits. Statement 4 is correct:(the company exception). So the correct combination is 1, 3 and 4 only.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the status and service conditions of the CVC:

1. The Central Vigilance Commissioner enjoys the salary of a Judge of the Supreme Court.
2. A Vigilance Commissioner's conditions are similar to those of a UPSC member.
3. These conditions cannot be varied to the disadvantage of the incumbent after appointment.
4. The CVC is an independent statutory body that acts as the central authority for vigilance and preventing corruption in the Central Government and its public sector organisations.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: His conditions are similar to those of the UPSC Chairman. Statement 2 is correct: A Vigilance Commissioner's conditions are similar to those of a UPSC member. Statement 3 is correct: These conditions cannot be varied to the disadvantage of the incumbent after appointment. Statement 4 is correct. So the correct combination is 2, 3 and 4 only.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the CVC:

1. It can inquire, or cause an inquiry, on a reference made by the Central Government into offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 by its public servants.
2. It can inquire into complaints against members of All India Services serving in the Union and Group A officers of the Central Government.
3. It exercises superintendence over the DSPE (CBI) in the investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, including giving directions.
4. Its superintendence over the CBI extends to the administrative control of the CBI.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It can inquire, or cause an inquiry, on a reference made by the Central Government into offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 by its public servants. Statement 2 is correct: It can inquire into complaints against members of All India Services serving in the Union and Group A officers of the Central Government. Statement 3 is correct: It exercises superintendence over the DSPE (CBI) in the investigation of offences under the Prevention of Corruption Act, including giving directions. Statement 4 is incorrect: Administrative control stays with the Central Government. So the correct combination is 1, 2 and 3 only.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:

1. It reviews the progress of CBI investigations into offences alleged under the Prevention of Corruption Act, and also into conventional crimes such as murder.
2. It reviews the status of sanctions for prosecution pending with competent authorities, with the aim of cutting delays.
3. It advises the Central Government and its authorities on vigilance and anti-corruption matters referred to it.
4. The Central Government must consult the CVC when framing or amending rules on vigilance and disciplinary matters of Central Services and All India Services members.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: The review concerns corruption cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act. Statement 2 is correct: It reviews the status of sanctions for prosecution pending with competent authorities, with the aim of cutting delays. Statement 3 is correct: It advises the Central Government and its authorities on vigilance and anti-corruption matters referred to it. Statement 4 is correct. So the correct combination is 2, 3 and 4 only.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the jurisdiction of the CVC:

1. It covers members of the All India Services serving in connection with the affairs of the Union and Group A officers of the Central Government.
2. It covers officers of Scale III and above in public sector banks.
3. It covers chief executives, board executives and officers of E-8 level and above in Schedule A and B PSUs, and E-7 and above in Schedule C and D PSUs.
4. In the Reserve Bank of India and NABARD it covers every employee, irrespective of grade.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: It covers members of the All India Services serving in connection with the affairs of the Union and Group A officers of the Central Government. Statement 2 is incorrect: The level is Scale V and above. Statement 3 is correct: It covers chief executives, board executives and officers of E-8 level and above in Schedule A and B PSUs, and E-7 and above in Schedule C and D PSUs. Statement 4 is incorrect: It covers officers of Grade D and above. So the correct combination is 1 and 3 only.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the working of the CVC:

1. It has no powers of a civil court, and its proceedings are administrative in character.
2. It may call for information, records or reports from the Central Government or its authorities to exercise general supervision over vigilance work.
3. After an inquiry by any agency on its reference, the agency itself decides the further course of action without reverting to the CVC.
4. It superintends vigilance administration in Central ministries and authorities, including PSUs and autonomous bodies.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: It has all the powers of a civil court and its proceedings are judicial in nature. Statement 2 is correct: It may call for information, records or reports from the Central Government or its authorities to exercise general supervision over vigilance work. Statement 3 is incorrect: The agency reports to the CVC, which advises on the next step. Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014:

1. The Act provides a mechanism for protecting the identity of whistle blowers.
2. The competent authority to receive disclosures under the Act is the Prime Minister's Office.
3. A false or frivolous complaint may be punished with imprisonment up to five years and a fine up to Rs 1 lakh.
4. The Act applies to the Special Protection Group.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: At present it is the Central Vigilance Commission. Statement 3 is incorrect: Up to two years in prison and a fine up to Rs 30,000. Statement 4 is incorrect: The Act is not applicable to the Special Protection Group. So exactly 1 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 1 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the CVC's complaint and jurisdiction rules:

1. The CVC is the only designated agency empowered to act against complainants who file motivated, malicious or vexatious complaints.
2. Under the Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers' Resolution, 2004 the CVC inquires into complaints and keeps the informer's identity confidential.
3. In the insurance sector the CVC covers senior divisional managers and above in general insurance companies and managers and above in LIC.
4. In societies and local authorities owned or controlled by the Centre, the CVC covers officers drawing Rs 8,700 a month (pre-revised) and above on the Central DA pattern.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The CVC is the only designated agency empowered to act against complainants who file motivated, malicious or vexatious complaints. Statement 2 is correct: Under the Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers' Resolution, 2004 the CVC inquires into complaints and keeps the informer's identity confidential. Statement 3 is incorrect: It is managers and above in general insurance companies and senior divisional managers and above in LIC. Statement 4 is correct. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Match the CVC component or instrument in List-I with its description in List-II
List-I
A. Chief Technical Examiners' Wing
B. Commissioners for Departmental Inquiries
C. Secretariat
D. Whistle Blowers' Resolution
List-II
1. Secretary, Joint Secretaries, Deputy Secretaries and Under Secretaries
2. Inquiry into complaints made by informers, with the informer's identity kept confidential and protected
3. Oral inquiries in departmental proceedings against public servants
4. Technical audit of construction works from a vigilance angle
questions.e: The Chief Technical Examiners' Wing does technical audit of construction works (A-4); the Commissioners for Departmental Inquiries conduct oral inquiries (B-3); the Secretariat is the staff of Secretary, Joint Secretaries, Deputy Secretaries and Under Secretaries (C-1); and the 2004 Resolution on Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers, the whistle-blowers' instrument, provides for inquiry into informers' complaints with their identity protected (D-2).
w: Swaps the technical wing and the Commissioners for Departmental Inquiries.
Swaps the Secretariat and the 2004 Resolution.
Swaps the technical wing and the Secretariat.
